newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Southern African summer seen dry, hot.
newsitem.headline: Southern African summer seen dry, hot.

text.p: Most parts of southern Africa should experience a dry and hot summer with below average rainfall expected in the months from November to January 1997, according to Mark Jury of the University of Cape Town's Oceanography Department.

In South Africa, the North-West and Free State provinces were likely to receive 50 percent less rain than normal, while rainfall in Gauteng, Mpumalanga and the Northern Province was expected to be 70 percent below normal.
However, rains in the Eastern Cape were seen rising 26 percent above normal, Jury said.

Northern Namibia would also be hit by 70 percent less rainfall than normal. Zimbabwe would, however, experience near normal rainfall dipping just 12 percent below normal and northern Tanzania, in the period October to December, would see rainfall of six percent below normal, Jury said.
Swaziland's rainfall in the period January to March was expected to be well above normal.
Jury warned that the incidence of malaria in eastern South Africa would rise to 119 percent above normal. --Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
